丶.note: A single dot: a drop, a spark, a mark.

氵.note: 水 squeezed onto the left side of a character: three drops of water.

扌.note: 手 squeezed onto the left side of a character.

冫.note: Two drops frozen solid: ice, cold. One drop fewer than 氵, water.

灬.note: 火 spread out along the bottom of a character as four dots.

宀.note: A roof with a chimney on top: a house.

穴.note: A roof (宀) over something split open (八): a cave, a hole.

艹.note: Two tufts of grass sprouting along the top of a character: plants.

辶.note: A road running under the character from the left: moving along.

攵.note: A hand holding a stick: striking, making something happen.

禾.note: A stalk of rice bowing under its ear: grain, the harvest.

阝.note: On the left of a character: a hill, or a flight of steps. The same shape on the right, おおざと, means a village.

广.note: A roof with one wall: a building open on one side.

疒.note: A sickbed propped against a wall: illness.

尸.note: A body stretched out, or a flag on a pole. In many kanji it simply roofs over what is below.

厶.note: A small closed loop, shaped like katakana ム: oneself, something private.

馬.note: A horse, mane flying, with four legs (灬) below.

欠.note: A person with their mouth wide open: yawning, gaping — and lacking.

頁.note: A big head on a small body. On the right of a character it means head.

牜.note: 牛 squeezed onto the left side, its bottom stroke flicked up.

羊.note: Horns on top, a woolly body below. Inside other kanji its tail is often cut short.

斤.note: An axe, blade down, handle to the right.

米.note: Grains of rice scattered around a cross.

里.note: Rice field (田) over earth (土): farmland, a village.

王.note: Three levels — heaven, people, earth — joined by one line: a king. On the left of a character it is usually 玉, a jewel, with its dot dropped.

石.note: A rock (口) tumbling down a cliff.

矢.note: An arrow, feathered end at the bottom.

匸.note: A box on its side, open to the right: somewhere to put things out of sight. In print it is almost the same as 匚, box, but dictionaries keep the two apart.

歹.note: A bare, broken bone: death, ruin.

己.note: A coiled thread, standing for oneself.

云.note: Two lines over a curl of vapour: a cloud, or words drifting out.

虫.note: A bug or a snake, head raised.

巾.note: A cloth hanging from a pole.

飠.note: 食 squeezed onto the left side of a character.

豕.note: A pig on its short legs.

耂.note: 老, old, cut down to its top half: an old man bent over his cane.

礻.note: 示, an altar, squeezed onto the left: gods, worship. Unlike 衤, clothing, it has one dot.

貝.note: A cowrie shell. Shells were once money, so as a part it means money or value.

糸.note: A twisted skein of silk. On the left of a character it is いとへん.

未.note: A tree (木) with a short extra branch: not grown yet. Read ミ, a sound it lends to 味, and マイ in 妹.

尺.note: An old unit of length, about a foot: a hand spread wide to measure.

弋.note: A stake with a hook on it, or an arrow on a cord.

开.note: Two posts under a crossbar. In 開 it is two hands lifting the bar off a gate.

丂.note: A stick with a kink near the top, like an old man's cane. Read コウ, a sound it lends to 考.

市.note: A lid (亠) over a cloth (巾): the awning over a market stall.

周.note: Earth (土) and a mouth (口) closed inside a frame (冂): a whole field, walked all the way round. Read シュウ, a sound it lends to 週.

廿.note: Two tens (十) joined along the bottom: twenty.

几.note: A low table on two legs. Wrapped round the outside of a character it is かぜがまえ, the frame of 風.

巴.note: A snake curled up with its head raised; also the comma-shaped swirl painted on Japanese drums.

反.note: A hand (又) pushing against a cliff. Read ハン, a sound it lends to 飯 and 坂.

斗.note: A dipper with a long handle, for scooping out and measuring grain.

也.note: An old grammar word, now seen mainly as the right side of 地 and 池, pond.

予.note: Read ヨ. In 野 it gives the sound ヤ.

化.note: A person (亻) beside a person upside down (匕): turning into something else. Read カ, a sound it lends to 花.

丁.note: A nail seen from the side. Read チョウ, a sound it lends to 町.

介.note: A person (人) standing between two lines. Read カイ, a sound it lends to 界.

首.note: A head with hair on top over a face with an eye.

官.note: A roof (宀) over rooms stacked one on the other: a government office. Read カン, a sound it lends to 館.

占.note: A divining rod (卜) over a mouth (口): reading fortunes. It also means to take up a spot.

至.note: An arrow landing point first in the ground (土): arriving. It sits under the roof in 室 and 屋.

尚.note: Sparkles (⺍) over a tall window: something held high. On top of 堂 its frame flattens into a crown.

廴.note: A road stretched long under the character from the left, like 辶 without its dots.

昜.note: The sun (日) rising over the horizon, its rays slanting down. The right side of 場, 陽 and 湯.

士.note: Like 土, earth, but with the upper bar the longer one. Read シ, a sound it lends to 仕.

亅.note: A stroke straight down with a hook flicked up at the foot.

罒.note: An eye (目) lying on its side along the top of a character: a net.

昔.note: Read セキ or シャク; it lends シャク to 借.

艮.note: 良, good, without its top dot.

卩.note: A person kneeling, or a seal stamped on a document. It sits on the right of a character.

勿.note: A banner with streamers flying. As a word it means do not. Read ブツ, a sound it lends to 物.

吏.note: Like 史, history, with a lid on top: the clerk who keeps the records.

乍.note: Shaped like a saw blade, teeth to the right. Read サク, a sound it lends to 作.

丙.note: The third of the old ten calendar signs: third place, grade C.

ク.note: Written like katakana ク: a person bent forward, as at the top of 急.

彐.note: Shaped like katakana ヨ. Its name comes from a pig's snout, but in many kanji, as in 急, it began as a hand.

帚.note: A hand (彐) gripping a broom whose bristles (巾) are bound under a band (冖).

癶.note: Two feet splayed apart along the top of a character, ready to set off.

业.note: Upright stakes in a row on a base: the top of 業. On its own it is the Chinese simplified form of 業.

免.note: Read メン. Inside 勉 its last stroke is cut short to make room for 力.

⺮.note: 竹, bamboo, squeezed onto the top of a character: two sprigs of leaves.

合.note: A lid (人) closing down over a mouth (口): two things that fit together.

是.note: The sun (日) over a foot planted squarely: correct, just so.

央.note: A big person (大) standing in the middle of a frame (冂). Read オウ, but in 英 and 映 it gives エイ.

与.note: A hand passing something over: give, hand over.

氏.note: A plant drooping over its roots: a family line. Read シ, a sound it lends to 紙.

亜.note: A squat, hunched frame: next-best, sub-. It also stands for Asia, once written 亜細亜.

口.mnemonic: Once a picture of an open mouth, squared off by the brush. As a part it is often just a box, a window or an opening.

目.mnemonic: Once a picture of an eye with its pupil, turned on end to fit a column of writing.

手.mnemonic: Once a picture of a hand: fingers spread across the top, the arm running down. On the left of other kanji it shrinks to 扌, as in 持.

足.mnemonic: Once a picture of a leg: a round kneecap (口) on top and a foot (止) planted on the ground below, its last stroke swept out.

体.mnemonic: Person (亻) + origin (本): the one thing every person starts out with and carries everywhere — the body.

心.mnemonic: Once a picture of a heart. At the bottom of a character it keeps this shape, as in 思 and 意; on the left it stands up as 忄.

思.mnemonic: A rice field (田) weighing on the heart (心): the farmer's mind is always out in the field — think.

考.mnemonic: An old man (耂) leaning on a bent stick (丂), stopping to think things over. 丂 is read コウ, and so is 考.

知.mnemonic: Arrow (矢) + mouth (口): someone who knows answers straight and fast, words flying from the mouth like an arrow.

意.mnemonic: Sound (音) + heart (心): the sound your heart makes — what you really mean, what you intend.

私.mnemonic: Grain (禾) + private (厶): the share of the harvest you keep back for yourself — private, and so I, me.

自.mnemonic: Once a picture of a nose. People point at their nose to mean themselves, so it came to mean self. It is 目, eye, with one extra stroke on top.

者.mnemonic: An old man (耂) sitting out in the sun (日): nobody in particular, just someone — a person.

主.mnemonic: Once a picture of an oil lamp: a flame (丶) burning on its stand (王). Whoever keeps the house's lamp lit is its master.

親.mnemonic: Stand (立) up in a tree (木) to see (見) further: a parent watching the road for their child to come home.

家.mnemonic: A roof (宀) over a pig (豕): the farm family keeps its pig safe under its own roof — house, home.

族.mnemonic: A flag flying from a flagpole (方), a bundle of arrows (矢) beneath it: the fighters of one clan gathered under their banner — tribe, family.

兄.mnemonic: A big mouth (口) on legs (儿): the older brother, always telling the younger ones what to do.

弟.mnemonic: A little boy with two tufts of hair (丷) winding a bow (弓) round a stick (丨): the younger brother, playing at hunters.

姉.mnemonic: Woman (女) + market (市): the older sister is the one trusted to go to the market with the money.

妹.mnemonic: Woman (女) + not yet (未): a girl not yet grown up — the younger sister. 未 lends its sound, as マイ.

朝.mnemonic: The sun (日) coming up through the grass (十, above and below it) while the moon (月) is still in the sky: morning.

昼.mnemonic: Measure (尺) how high the sun (日) stands over the horizon (一): as high as it goes — noon, daytime.

夕.mnemonic: Once a picture of a crescent moon just risen: evening. Careful — it looks almost exactly like katakana タ.

夜.mnemonic: Under a lid (亠) of darkness, a person (亻) walks home by the evening (夕) moon, the stroke across it their long shadow: night.

早.mnemonic: A sunflower: a face like the sun (日) on a stem (十) with two leaves, first to open each day — early.

曜.mnemonic: The sun (日) and a bird (隹) with its wings (羽) spread: the sun, the moon and the planets flying across the sky one after another, each lending its name to a day of the week.

週.mnemonic: A circuit (周) along the road (辶): once round all seven days — a week. 周 is read シュウ, and so is 週.

度.mnemonic: In a hall (广), twenty (廿) hands (又) go up to be counted, again and again: how many times, and by how many degrees.

代.mnemonic: A person (亻) standing in for a stake (弋) while it is replaced: a substitute — and each generation takes the place of the last.

計.mnemonic: Words (言) + ten (十): counting aloud up to ten on your fingers — measure, calculate.

春.mnemonic: Three (三) people (人) out enjoying the sun (日) for the first time in months: spring.

夏.mnemonic: A face (自) under a sun hat (一), on dragging legs (夂): someone trudging slowly through the heat — summer.

秋.mnemonic: Grain (禾) + fire (火): the harvest cut and the stubble burnt off in the fields — autumn.

冬.mnemonic: Dragging legs (夂) over ice (冫): trudging through the frozen months — winter.

風.mnemonic: A sail (几) swelling out, and an insect (虫) swept along beneath it: the wind.

色.mnemonic: A person leaning over a coiled snake (巴): their face changes colour at the sight. 色 is colour, and also the look on a face.

赤.mnemonic: Earth (土) over a fire, its flames flicking out on both sides: the ground glowing red. It began as big (大) over fire (火).

青.mnemonic: A sprout (生, pressed flat on top) over the moon (月): the green of new leaves and the blue of the night sky, both 青 in Japanese. 生 lends its sound, セイ.

黒.mnemonic: A village (里) with fires (灬) burning under it: everything covered in soot — black.

茶.mnemonic: Grass (艹) over a person (人) resting under a tree (木): picking leaves in the shade for tea.

犬.mnemonic: A big (大) animal with one ear pricked up (丶): a dog. The character began as a picture of a dog, stood on end.

牛.mnemonic: Once a picture of a cow's head seen from the front: two horns sticking up and a line down the face. On the left of other kanji it becomes 牜.

魚.mnemonic: Once a picture of a fish standing on its nose: the head on top, a scaly body (田), and the tail fin (灬) spread at the bottom.

鳥.mnemonic: Once a picture of a bird: a head with an eye at the top, a body, and claws (灬) along the bottom. Leave out the eye and it becomes 烏, the crow — too black for its eye to show.

肉.mnemonic: Once a picture of a slab of meat (冂) on the block, marbled with streaks of fat (人). Squeezed into other kanji, meat is written 月.

飲.mnemonic: Eat (飠) + a mouth gaping wide (欠): head tipped back, gulping it down — drink.

飯.mnemonic: Eat (飠) + turn over (反): rice turned over in the pot until it is cooked — a meal. 反 is read ハン, and so is 飯.

料.mnemonic: Rice (米) + a ladle (斗): scooping out a measure of rice — the materials for a meal, or the fee paid in grain.

理.mnemonic: A jewel (王) from the village (里), cut along the lines in the stone: following its grain, its logic — reason. 里 is read リ, and so is 理.

味.mnemonic: Mouth (口) + not yet (未): the fruit is not yet ripe, and your mouth knows it — taste. 未 is read ミ, and so is 味.

地.mnemonic: Earth (土), and also (也) more earth, spreading as far as you can see: the ground, the land.

海.mnemonic: Water (氵) every (毎) way you look: the sea.

空.mnemonic: A hole (穴) dug out with a tool (工): nothing left inside — empty. The biggest empty space of all is the sky.

野.mnemonic: A village (里) with land set aside beforehand (予) all around it: the open fields. 予 is read ヨ, close to the ヤ of 野.

花.mnemonic: Grass (艹) that changes (化): a green bud turning into a flower. 化 is read カ, and so is 花.

田.mnemonic: Once a picture of a rice field, cut into four paddies by the raised paths between them.

町.mnemonic: Rice field (田) + a nail (丁): fields staked out into blocks, then built on — a town. 丁 is read チョウ, and so is 町.

京.mnemonic: Once a picture of a tall building on a mound: a roof (亠), a window (口), and pillars (小) beneath. Where the tall buildings stand is the capital.

世.mnemonic: It began as three tens (十) joined into one: thirty years, a generation. All the generations together are the world.

界.mnemonic: Rice field (田) + between (介): the ridge between one field and the next — a boundary. Everything inside the boundaries is your world. 介 is read カイ, and so is 界.

道.mnemonic: A head (首) moving along a road (辶): the road you follow, and the way you go.

図.mnemonic: A frame (囗) with a few marks (⺍) and an X (メ) inside: a treasure map — a map, a diagram.

駅.mnemonic: Horse (馬) + measure (尺): the old post stations stood a measured distance apart, where riders changed horses — a station.

館.mnemonic: Eat (飠) + official (官): the hall where visiting officials were fed and lodged — a large building. 官 is read カン, and so is 館.

店.mnemonic: A building open at the front (广) where a fortune-teller (占) has taken a spot and set up for business: a shop.

屋.mnemonic: A flag (尸) flying over the place you arrive (至) at the end of the day: a house, a roof — or a shop hanging out its sign.

室.mnemonic: A roof (宀) you arrive (至) under and stay: a room.

住.mnemonic: A person (亻) who is master (主) of the house: the one who lives there. 主 lends its sound too — シュ, ジュウ.

台.mnemonic: A nose (厶) over a mouth (口): a head set up on a stand for all to see — a stand, a platform.

堂.mnemonic: Something held in esteem (尚) raised on packed earth (土): a grand hall.

立.mnemonic: Once a picture of a person standing with arms spread and feet planted on the ground: the top is the head, the bottom line the ground — stand.

建.mnemonic: A brush (聿) drawing up the plans, and a long stride (廴) pacing out the ground: build.

場.mnemonic: Earth (土) in the sunshine (昜): an open patch of ground where people gather — a place.

工.mnemonic: Once a picture of a carpenter's square, the tool for ruling straight lines: craft, construction.

公.mnemonic: Open up (八) what is private (厶) and it belongs to everyone: public.

仕.mnemonic: A person (亻) who is a samurai (士): he serves his lord — serve, do. 士 is read シ, and so is 仕.

事.mnemonic: A mouth (口) at the top, and below it a hand gripping a brush hung on a barb (亅): the clerk writing down each matter as it is spoken — a thing, an affair.

会.mnemonic: People under one roof (人), talking (云): a meeting.

社.mnemonic: An altar (礻) on the earth (土): the shrine of the local god, where the village gathered — and so a company of people.

員.mnemonic: A mouth (口) over money (貝): one more mouth on the payroll — a member, an employee.

売.mnemonic: A samurai (士) fallen on hard times hangs a crown (冖) over his stall and stands on his legs (儿) all day: selling. Its old form, 賣, was 出, go out, over 買, buy.

買.mnemonic: A net (罒) bulging with shells (貝), the money of old: off to market to buy.

貸.mnemonic: Substitute (代) over money (貝): money that stands in for someone else's for a while — lend. 代 lends its sound as well: ダイ, タイ.

借.mnemonic: A person (亻) who borrowed it long ago (昔) and still has not given it back: borrow. 昔 can be read シャク, and so is 借.

銀.mnemonic: Metal (金) + stubborn (艮): the metal that stubbornly stays white instead of turning gold — silver.

服.mnemonic: A body (月) on the left; on the right a hand (又) helping a kneeling figure (卩) into a robe: clothes.

着.mnemonic: A sheep (羊), its tail swept aside, pulled right down over your eyes (目): wool to wear. Wrap up well and you will arrive, the other thing 着 means.

洋.mnemonic: Water (氵) with waves as white as a flock of sheep (羊): the ocean — and what came across it was Western. 羊 is read ヨウ, and so is 洋.

物.mnemonic: A cow (牜) decked out with a banner (勿) on market day: a thing up for trade. 勿 is read ブツ, and so is 物.

品.mnemonic: Three boxes (口) stacked in a shop window: goods, articles for sale.

使.mnemonic: A person (亻) ordering an official (吏) about, sending him off on their business: use.

用.mnemonic: A frame with two crossbars and a post driven down through the middle: a plain rack or fence, the sort of thing that is always in use.

作.mnemonic: A person (亻) at work with a saw (乍): making something. 乍 is read サク, and so is 作.

方.mnemonic: A signpost (亠) with one arm swinging out to the side: it points the way — direction. A way of doing things, and politely a person, grew out of that.

切.mnemonic: Seven (七), squeezed to the left, beside a sword (刀): seven slashes of the blade — cut.

元.mnemonic: Once a picture of a person on their legs (儿) with the head (二) picked out on top. The head is where it all starts: origin, beginning.

医.mnemonic: An arrow (矢) pulled out of a wound and hidden away (匸) where it can do no more harm: the doctor's work — medicine.

病.mnemonic: Sickness (疒) + third (丙): the third day in bed and still ill.

院.mnemonic: On a hill (阝), a great roof (宀) that has stood there since the beginning (元): an institution — a hospital, a school, a temple.

死.mnemonic: A person sitting (匕) beside a heap of bones (歹): death.

走.mnemonic: Earth (土) kicked up by a foot (止) pushing off hard: run. On the left and bottom of 起 it still means running.

歩.mnemonic: Stop (止), then on a little (少) more, and again: walking, one step at a time.

止.mnemonic: Once a picture of a foot, toes to the right, planted on the ground: stop. As a part it often still means foot, as in 走 and 歩.

起.mnemonic: Run (走) + self (己): you get yourself up and running — rise, wake up. 己 is read キ, and so is 起.

急.mnemonic: A person (ク) with a hand (彐) grabbing at their back, heart (心) pounding: hurry.

帰.mnemonic: A broom (帚) leaning against the doorpost (刂): back home, and time to sweep up — return.

去.mnemonic: Earth (土) heaped over something private (厶): you bury your secret and walk away from it — leave, the past.

送.mnemonic: Hands waving (丷) under the open sky (天) as someone sets off down the road (辶): seeing them off, sending.

通.mnemonic: A road (辶) you use (用) every day: the one you pass through on your commute. The hook on top, like katakana マ, is the ticket gate.

持.mnemonic: A hand (扌) + temple (寺): holding the temple's offerings carefully in your hand. 寺 is read ジ, and so is 持 — as in 時.

力.mnemonic: An arm bent at the elbow, flexing its muscle: power, strength. As a part, in 男 and 動, it brings the muscle with it.

動.mnemonic: Heavy (重) + power (力): it takes power to move something heavy.

運.mnemonic: Carts (車) under covers (冖) rolling down the road (辶): carrying goods. Whether they arrive safely is down to luck, the other meaning of 運.

転.mnemonic: A wheel (車) spinning so fast it throws up a cloud (云) of dust: turn, roll.

発.mnemonic: Feet planted wide (癶) over two (二) legs (儿) crouched at the starting line: ready, steady — depart.

始.mnemonic: A woman (女) steps up onto the stage (台), and the show begins.

終.mnemonic: Thread (糸) + winter (冬): the last thread of the year wound up as winter comes — the end.

開.mnemonic: Two hands (开) lifting the bar off a gate (門): open.

待.mnemonic: Going (彳) to the temple (寺), where you stand in line and wait your turn. The same 寺 sits in 時 and 持.

集.mnemonic: Once a picture of birds (隹) settling in a tree (木) — three of them in the oldest form: gather.

教.mnemonic: An old man (耂) with a stick in his hand (攵), standing over a child (子): teaching, the old-fashioned way.

習.mnemonic: Wings (羽) flapping again and again above something white (白) — a fledgling on the edge of its nest, practising until it learns to fly.

勉.mnemonic: There is no escape (免) from it, so put all your power (力) in: effort. With 強, strong, it makes 勉強, study.

強.mnemonic: A bow (弓) strung with silk from an insect (虫) spinning in its own private (厶) cocoon: the string never snaps — strong.

業.mnemonic: A row of stakes (业) penning in a sheep (羊), a woodpile (木) underneath: the whole farm at work — a trade, business.

問.mnemonic: A mouth (口) at the gate (門), calling out to whoever is inside: asking a question. 門 lends its sound, モン, and dictionaries file it under the mouth.

題.mnemonic: Just so (是) — the right words — written at the head (頁) of the page: a title, a topic.

答.mnemonic: A bamboo (⺮) tally split in two: the halves fit (合) back together the way an answer fits its question.

試.mnemonic: Words (言) held up against a carpenter's square (工) before the stake (弋) goes in: checking whether they are true — try, test.

験.mnemonic: A horse (馬) led under the roof (人) of the market, where the buyer opens its mouth (口) to check its teeth: testing, verifying.

研.mnemonic: Stone (石) + two hands lifting (开): working a blade back and forth over a whetstone — sharpen, polish, and so study hard.

究.mnemonic: A hole (穴) dug nine (九) levels deep: research goes all the way to the bottom. 九 is read キュウ, and so is 究.

質.mnemonic: Two axes (斤) laid on the counter for money (貝): tools left as a pledge at the pawnshop, weighed for what they are really worth — quality.

正.mnemonic: Stop (止) at the line (一) and stay on the right side of it: correct.

注.mnemonic: Water (氵) + master (主): the master of the house pours the tea while every guest watches — pour, and pay attention.

言.mnemonic: Lines of words rising out of a mouth (口): say. On the left of a character it becomes ごんべん, the speech radical, as in 話 and 試.

文.mnemonic: Once a picture of a person, head (亠) on top, with a crossed pattern (乂) tattooed on the chest: a mark, a pattern — and so writing.

字.mnemonic: A child (子) under a roof (宀), learning to write at home: letters, characters. 子 is read シ; 字 is ジ.

漢.mnemonic: Water (氵) with grass (艹) thick on its banks, and a mouth (口) calling across it: the Han, the river that named a dynasty, and so China — and 漢字.

英.mnemonic: Grass (艹) + centre (央): the finest flower at the heart of the plant — excellent. Its sound, エイ, was borrowed to write England, and so English.

歌.mnemonic: "Possible (可), possible (可)!" sung out through a wide-open mouth (欠): a song. 可 lends its sound, カ.

音.mnemonic: Stand (立) over the sun (日): the rooster stands up at sunrise and makes a noise — sound.

楽.mnemonic: Once a picture of a drum (白) on a wooden (木) stand, with strings stretched out on either side: music, and the pleasure it brings.

映.mnemonic: Sun (日) + centre (央): the sun in the middle of the sky, shining back off every window — reflect, project. 央 gives it the sound エイ, as in 英.

画.mnemonic: A rice field (田) in an open box (凵), a line (一) ruled across the top: a map with its borders drawn in — a picture, and a plan.

旅.mnemonic: Once a picture of a flag on its pole (方), with a band of people marching beneath it: soldiers on the move, and then any traveller — a journey.

写.mnemonic: Under the photographer's hood (冖), the camera gives (与) back what it sees: copy, photograph.

真.mnemonic: Ten (十) eyes (目) up on a stand with legs (八), all looking at the same thing: with ten witnesses, it must be true.

紙.mnemonic: Thread (糸) + clan (氏): fibres pressed flat into sheets for the family records — paper. 氏 is read シ, and so is 紙.

有.mnemonic: A hand (ナ) holding a piece of meat (月): having something — have, exist.

多.mnemonic: Evening (夕) on top of evening (夕): night after night piling up — many.

少.mnemonic: Small (小), and then a slash (丿) takes a piece of it away: fewer still — few, a little.

重.mnemonic: A thousand (千) villages (里) stacked up on one another: heavy.

広.mnemonic: A building (广) with only one small private (厶) corner taken up: the rest is open floor — wide, spacious.

近.mnemonic: Road (辶) + axe (斤): the woodcutter's axe is only a short walk down the road — near. 斤 is read キン, and so is 近.

新.mnemonic: Stand (立) a tree (木) up and take an axe (斤) to it: fresh-cut wood — new.

古.mnemonic: A story passed through ten (十) mouths (口), one generation after another: old.

安.mnemonic: A woman (女) at home under a roof (宀): all is calm and safe. In Japanese it also came to mean cheap.

明.mnemonic: Sun (日) + moon (月): the two brightest things in the sky side by side — bright.

悪.mnemonic: A second-rate (亜) heart (心): bad, evil.

不.mnemonic: A bird shooting straight up into the sky (一), wings folded back: it does not come down again — not.

同.mnemonic: Inside one frame (冂), one (一) line and one mouth (口): everyone saying exactly the same thing.

別.mnemonic: A mouth (口), power (力) and a knife (刂): someone strong enough to cut one piece clean away from another — separate, part.

特.mnemonic: A cow (牜) led to the temple (寺): the one chosen for the festival — special. 寺 is its sound part, though here it has worn into トク.

以.mnemonic: A hooked plough-blade marked with a dot (丶), and a person (人) pushing it: working by means of a tool. It marks a starting point — 以上 from here up, 以下 from here down.
